title: The First of Adab: Eating with the Right Hand and Du'a
summary: Among the Prophetic adab is eating with the right hand, saying 'Bismillah,' and contentment. Teach your child these adab through play and gentleness, not harshness; adab planted with love endures.
try_this: This week: Gently remind your child to eat with their right hand, and praise them whenever they do.
reflection_prompts: Which adab has your child begun to master?
Is the atmosphere around teaching filled with rifq?

review_defects.why: The Arabic uses 'اللطف' (al-lutf, gentleness), not 'الرفق' (al-rifq). The translation introduces the transliterated term 'rifq' which is not present in the source, then explains it as gentleness. This substitutes a different Arabic word and creates inconsistency with the rest of the document where 'لطف' is translated as 'gently'.

review_defects.english: Is the atmosphere around teaching filled with rifq?
review_defects.why: The Arabic asks if the atmosphere is 'لطيفة' (gentle/kind). The English changes this to 'filled with rifq', again introducing the term 'rifq' not used in the source and altering the phrasing from a simple adjective to a metaphorical 'filled with' construction.
